requested.title: Image src derived from request origin, while the site-wide SSRF private-network guard is disabled for this demo
Unauthenticated, unthrottled hard cache invalidation affecting all visitors
getRequestContext() in a Handle throws on unmatched URLs under /demos/mode-watcher*, leaking a stack trace and bypassing the error pipeline
Unauthenticated page triggers ~20ms of blocking CPU per request with no rate limit or caching
OG render cache is gated on MOCHI_DOCKER, so the CPU-heavy card endpoint is fully uncached in non-container production
Unpublished draft blog posts resolve to public, long-lived OG cards in the deployed container

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The finding's central premise — that `sourceUrl()`'s origin is request-derived — is false in effect for this site. I traced `getRequestContext().url` to `buildRequestContext` (runtime/requestSetup.ts L89), which sets `url = buildPublicUrl(req, cfg.proxy)`; `buildPublicUrl` calls `resolveExpectedOrigin`, whose very first statement is `if (options?.origin) return options.origin;` (runtime/proxy.ts L58-60). `packages/site/src/index.ts` L201 passes `proxy: { origin, … }` unconditionally, with `origin` computed at L116-118 from `MOCHI_DOMAIN`/`MOCHI_PORT` env (defaulting to `http://localhost:3333`). So `url.origin` is a deployment constant and the `Host` header can never reach it — there is no header-controlled value entering the sealed image token, and the index.ts comment's invariant (server-minted, not user input) holds, even if the word 'hardcoded' is loose. The finding concedes this itself ('Current exploitability: mitigated'), so it describes a hypothetical future refactor, not a vulnerability. I also tested the propagation argument and it fails: `demoIndex.ts` (the published 'index.ts') sets no `blockPrivateNetworks: false`, and the default is `true` (image/config.ts L100), while `resolvePublicUrl` rejects the literal hostname `localhost` before any DNS work (utils/publicUrl.ts L85-87) — so a copied recipe's demo breaks with a 400 on first use rather than silently becoming an SSRF. The residual variant (arbitrary *public* host) is a fixed-path `GET …/demos/image-invalidation/source.jpg` toward a host the attacker already controls, with `redirect: 'manual'` re-validation per hop, AAD-bound tokens, a size cap and a non-raster content-type downgrade (imageEndpoint.ts L25-30) — no private-network reach and no meaningful capability. At most this is a comment-accuracy nit plus a hardening suggestion (`image.allowedHosts`), not an exploitable finding.

The core mechanism checks out. `/demos/image-invalidation` is a public `Mochi.page` with a `default` action and no `rateLimit`; `packages/site`'s `Mochi.serve()` sets no global limiter (index.ts has no `rateLimit` key) and `protection.protect` is scoped to `/demos/protection*` only, so nothing throttles the POST. `invalidateImage(src, { hard: true })` → `cache.invalidateOriginal(src, true)` (image/imageCache.ts L330-352) does `cascadeSource()` then `delete(origKey)`, evicting the placeholder and *every configured size's* variant — ~20 entries for this site's `image.sizes` map. `generation` is module-global, so one anonymous POST bumps the `&g=` nonce for all visitors, and Origin-only `csrfCheck` is indeed no obstacle to a scripted `curl` with a spoofed `Origin`. Sibling demo POST actions in the same repo (`reload-form-data`, `queue`) do carry `{limit: 60, window: '1m', skip: req.method !== 'POST'}`, so this route deviates from the project's own convention — that is the real, actionable defect. Two claims are wrong, which is why I'm downgrading severity. First, the page GET does *not* perform the loopback fetch or the four transforms: `getImageUrl` → `mintFor` → `mintImageUrl` only runs `encryptImageRequest` (image/imageApi.ts L48, L86-101) — all fetch/decode work happens on the separate `/_mochi/image/*` requests, so the attacker needs 5 requests per cycle, not 2, and the render never blocks on it. Second, the deployed container runs `development: true`, where `resolveImageCacheControl` deliberately emits no `Cache-Control` for images (image/imageEndpoint.ts L45-50), so there is little browser cache for the nonce to bust. What remains is a modest unauthenticated CPU-amplification and a global counter mutable by anonymous users, on demo code whose advertised purpose is exactly this button — a low-priority hardening bug, not a MEDIUM security issue.

I verified every link in this chain. `composedFetch` (Mochi.ts L1863-1935) builds its `MochiEvent` and calls `middleware({ event, resolve: innerResolve })` at L1922 with **no** `requestContext.run` anywhere on that path and no try/catch around it — contrast the page path at L977 and the api path at L1207, which both wrap `middleware` inside `requestContext.run(ctx, …)`. `getRequestContext()` throws when `getStore()` is undefined (runtime/requestContext.ts L183-187), and `assertServerOnly` is a no-op on the server (utils/serverOnly.ts L16-20), so nothing short-circuits the throw. The site's handle chain is `sequence(compress, immutableAssets, helloWorld, asciiDog, analytics, encodeDebugBarPaths, noCache, cookieVaryTestHandle, modeWatcherHandle, shotHandle)`; `sequence` (runtime/hooks.ts L102-131) has no try/catch, nor do `compress`/`noCache`/`analytics`/the site's own handles, so the rejection escapes `composedFetch`. I confirmed there is no catch-all: the only wildcard pattern in the whole site is `/og/*`, `options.fetch` is unset, and no `public/` file sits under that prefix — so `/demos/mode-watcher/x`, `/demos/mode-watcher/favicon.ico` and `/demos/mode-watcherX` are all unmatched and hit line 17 after only the `startsWith` test at line 14, before any cookie comparison. `Bun.serve()` at Mochi.ts L2020-2026 receives no `error` handler (and `options.development` is never injected into `bunOptions` — L479 computes a local only), so Bun's own default applies: the vendored types in this repo state `development` defaults to `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` and that development mode 'returns rendered error messages with stack traces instead of a generic 500 error' (bun-types/serve.d.ts L848-851, L1303-1309). The site image is built from `Dockerfile` per `.github/workflows/build.yml` (`site` leg, `dockerfile: Dockerfile`), whose ENTRYPOINT is `bun run dev:site` → `NODE_ENV=development bun src/index.ts`. So a single unauthenticated GET yields a 500 with a stack trace instead of the site 404, and skips `handleError`, the `request` event, `analytics()` and `compress()`. `demoLlms.test.ts` boots `Mochi.serve()` with `routes`/`queues` only and no `handle`, so nothing covers this. Keeping MEDIUM: trivially reachable, no preconditions, and it is the only route on the site that leaks a raw framework stack trace — a site that otherwise goes out of its way to scrub file paths (`encodeDebugBarPaths`).

Every factual claim holds. I measured the corpus: `robinson-crusoe.txt` is 643,438 bytes / 123,973 words, read once at module load and sliced into `BOOK`. `requestMemo` is strictly request-scoped — `requestCache.ts` keys off `ctx.requestCache` on the per-request `MochiRequestContext`, which `buildRequestContext` creates fresh and which dies with the request — so the memo collapses the five facet helpers within one render but never across requests. `/demos/request-cache` is a bare `Mochi.page('./src/demos/request-cache/RequestCache.svelte')` with no `serverProps`, no actions, and no `rateLimit`; the site's `Mochi.serve()` sets no global `rateLimit` (other routes do opt in — `/api/captcha-demo/*`, `charts`, `queue`, `rate-limit`), and `protection` only covers `/demos/protection*`. `noCache` sets `Cache-Control: no-cache` with no ETag, so no proxy absorbs repeats. `analyze()` is fully synchronous — `toLowerCase()` over 640 KB, a ~124k-match global regex, a 124k-insert Map, a second ~124k-match pass across ~10-15k sentences, then a sort — and Bun runs handlers on one JS thread, so each hit blocks the event loop for every other in-flight request (the author's own comment estimates 16-25 ms; my read of the work suggests that is conservative). The `prefetch` speculation rule at `href_matches: '/*'`, eagerness `moderate`, does not exclude this path, so link hover alone triggers a full SSR render. The recomputation is also genuinely pointless: `BOOK` is a module constant and no request data feeds `analyze`. Keeping MEDIUM rather than treating this as excluded demo code: unlike the enumerated demo shortcuts (hardcoded `hunter2`, shared module state, missing auth), the impact here is event-loop starvation that degrades the whole deployed site, a single cheap GET is the whole attack, and the fix (a per-route `rateLimit`, already used by siblings) does not alter what the demo demonstrates.

The precondition for the attack — a production deployment where `MOCHI_DOCKER !== 'true'` — does not exist. `.github/workflows/build.yml` builds the `site` leg from `Dockerfile` (`dockerfile: Dockerfile`), and that Dockerfile sets `ENV MOCHI_DOCKER=true`, so in the shipped deployment `IS_DOCKER` is true, `getOgCard` goes through `MochiCache` (og/cache.ts L20), and `og/routes.ts` L37-42 emits `public, max-age=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800` plus an `ETag` and short-circuits on `If-None-Match`. The finding concedes this ('In the Docker deployment that is actually shipped today this is mitigated'); `bun run start` is a local convenience script, not a deployment path in this repo. I also disagree that the guard contradicts its comment: the comment says 'The key covers the subject, not the drawing code, so only the deployed container caches' — because `RENDERER_VERSION` is bumped by hand, a dev who edits `render.ts`/`cards.ts`/`background.ts` without bumping it would be served a stale card, so 'skip the cache everywhere except the deployed container' is precisely the stated intent and `MOCHI_DOCKER` is exactly the 'am I the deployed container' signal. Switching the gate to `NODE_ENV === 'development'` as recommended would in fact *enable* caching in the deployed container only incidentally — that container runs `NODE_ENV=development`, so the suggested replacement would turn the cache off in production. Finally, a per-IP limiter (`{ limit: 120, window: '1m' }`, og/routes.ts L46) applies in every mode, and the noise tile is memoized (`tile ??= noiseTile()`) so only the first render pays for it, while `canvas.encode()` is off-thread in @napi-rs/canvas. Legitimate code-quality observation about using a container marker as a production marker; not an exploitable vulnerability.

The logic flaw is real and precisely diagnosed. `DEVELOPMENT = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` (og/resolve.ts L7) is true in production: build.yml deploys the `site` leg from `Dockerfile`, whose ENTRYPOINT `bun run dev:site` resolves to `NODE_ENV=development bun src/index.ts`, and the Dockerfile comment says so deliberately. `getPost(slug, { includeDrafts: true })` therefore returns `draft: true` entries (lib/blog.ts L107-116, which only null-checks drafts when `includeDrafts` is falsy), `resolveOgSubject` hands back `{ kind: 'blog', title, date }`, and og/routes.ts L37-38 returns a 200 JPEG with `public, max-age=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800` plus an ETag — so the card is publicly cacheable for up to 7 days and the server-side `MochiCache` holds it for `maxTimeToLive: 604_800_000` ms. The finding is also right that `noCache` leaves a route's own `Cache-Control` alone, and that routes.ts L229/L241 carry the identical flaw. I'm downgrading severity for three reasons. First, it is latent: `packages/site/src/blog/` contains four posts and none has `draft:` frontmatter, so nothing is leaking today. Second, the confidentiality value of the gate is near zero for this project — the repo is public (packages/cli/src/download.ts pulls `https://codeload.github.com/khromov/mochi/tar.gz/<ref>` with, in its own words, 'no auth'), so a draft's full markdown is already readable on GitHub; `draft: true` is an editorial publication flag, not a secrecy control. Third, the incremental exposure at this file is a title and a date, strictly less than the page routes in the same container that already render the whole draft body and list it on `/blog/`. Real bug worth fixing (gate drafts on something that is false in the deployed image, and refuse to emit a cacheable response for a draft subject), but not a MEDIUM information-disclosure.
